t: The Ptolemaic Kingdom was a Macedonian dynasty that ruled Egypt as pharaohs from Alexandria for nearly three centuries.
Nile grain made it rich, and Alexandria's Library, Mouseion and Pharos made it the intellectual capital of the Hellenistic world.
Dynastic feuds, native revolts and Roman meddling wore it down; after Actium, Rome annexed Egypt in 30 BCE.
dyk: The Rosetta Stone, the key to deciphering hieroglyphs, records a Ptolemaic priestly decree of 196 BCE written in hieroglyphic, demotic and Greek.
ev: Ptolemy becomes satrap of Egypt after the death of Alexander the Great
Ptolemy I Soter proclaims himself king, founding the dynasty
Ptolemy II Philadelphus begins his reign over an empire reaching Cyprus and the Aegean
Ptolemy IV defeats Antiochus III at Raphia with a phalanx of native Egyptians
A great native revolt disrupts Upper Egypt
Priests issue the decree later inscribed on the Rosetta Stone
Octavian defeats Cleopatra VII and Mark Antony at Actium
Rome annexes Egypt, ending the Ptolemaic state
